name: The Fairmont San Francisco
positioning: Fairmont San Francisco, a Beaux Arts hotel atop Nob Hill with rooms in a historic Main Building and a contemporary Tower
best_for: Travelers who want a historic Nob Hill base with Bay views
Families wanting larger rooms that sleep up to six

facts.text: The hotel is a Beaux Arts landmark atop Nob Hill.
Guestrooms and suites are split between a historic Main Building and a contemporary Tower.
Fairmont 2 Queen rooms in the main building have 14-ft vaulted ceilings and windows that open, with city or interior views.
Signature Bay View rooms have Bay views through large picture windows, with landmarks including Alcatraz, Coit Tower and the Golden Gate Bridge.
The Penthouse spans the entire 8th floor and has a library, billiards room and outdoor terrace with skyline and Bay views.
Family Rooms in the main building can accommodate up to 6 adults.
The One Bedroom Suite with balcony has French doors leading to a balcony overlooking the rooftop garden.
Laurel Court is a dining room serving breakfast, lunch and dinner under high ceilings and chandeliers.
Afternoon Tea at the hotel has been a tradition since 1907.

highlights.text: The Tony Bennett Suite pays homage to Tony Bennett, who first performed his signature tune in the hotel in 1961.
The Tonga Room & Hurricane Bar serves tiki cocktails and pu pu platters.
Signature Bay View Suites are on floors 2-9 and have large picture windows and telescopes.
The hotel has a rooftop garden with a fountain and views of the city.
The hotel has its own beehives and allows pets.

considerations.text: Overnight valet parking for guests carries a fee.
Fairmont 1 Queen rooms are interior rooms in the historic main building.
WhataHotel notes the historic building has some rooms showing age.

sources.title: Condé Nast Traveler: Fairmont San Francisco
